statements.statement: The PLOS ONE editors issued an Expression of Concern to inform readers of unresolved issues, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached.

The notice reports an apparent vertical discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 panel between 293T and A549 lanes; Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the Results statement that LSD1 siRNA reduced H460 migration is not supported.

The notice says the paper does not describe the controls for the Flag-LSD1 and LSD1 siRNA transfection experiments in enough detail to replicate them, while the abstract states interrupting LSD1 with siRNA or pargyline suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion of A549, H460 and 293T cells.

The notice says similarities with other groups' work call into question validity and provenance, but does not name the patient-tissue or survival analyses (Figs. 1–3, Table 1) among its specific issues.

Section 2 of the draft cites Lv et al. for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue than normal in resected samples from 80 NSCLC patients, which the paper reports; the notice does not name these tissue analyses but says similarities with other groups' work call validity and provenance into question.
Section 3 cites Lv et al. [12] for a scratch-assay result of reduced H460 migration after LSD1 siRNA, and the draft takes this as the clearest indication that LSD1 is a driver of migration.

The paper states H460 migration was gradually reduced after LSD1 siRNA, but the notice says Fig. 7 does not report LSD1 siRNA data so the statement is not supported, and the controls for transfection experiments are not described in enough detail to replicate.

The Section 3 use carries most weight because the draft says its main evidence is a single cell-line study; the editors issued an Expression of Concern and the authors did not respond or could not be reached.

Section 3 cites Lv et al. [12] for a scratch-assay result of reduced H460 migration after LSD1 siRNA, taken as the clearest indication LSD1 drives migration, but the notice says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment so the result is not supported.

Section 2 cites Lv et al. for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue in 80 NSCLC patients; the notice does not name patient-tissue or survival analyses among its issues, but the editors issued an Expression of Concern and the notice says similarities with other groups' work call validity and provenance into question.
